explain.say: Some numbers are huge. Light travels about 300,000,000 metres every second. Writing all those zeros is slow and easy to get wrong. Look at our number: 45 million. Let us make it neat.

explain.say: First, move the decimal point so the number is between 1 and 10. 45,000,000 becomes 4.5. Look at the second box. Why not 45? Because 45 is bigger than 10.

explain.say: Now count how many places the point jumped. It started at the end, after the last zero, and moved to just after the 4. That is 7 places. Can you count them?

stages.ask: What does the power of 10 tell you?

explain.say: So 45 million is 4.5 times 10 to the power 7. 10 to the 7 means multiply by 10 seven times. That is standard form: a number from 1 to under 10, times a power of 10.

explain.say: Fantastic! Tiny numbers use negative powers. A germ is about 1 times 10 to the minus 6 metres long, a millionth of a metre. Wow: the Earth weighs about 6 times 10 to the 24 kilograms! Challenge: write 3,200 in standard form.

faq.q: How do you write a number in standard form?
faq.a: Move the decimal point to make a number from 1 to under 10, then count the jumps. 45,000,000 is 4.5 times 10 to the 7.
asks: What are the steps for standard form?

faq.q: What does the power of 10 tell you?
faq.a: It tells you how many places the decimal point moves. A positive power means a big number, a negative power means a small one.
asks: What does the 10 to the 7 mean?

faq.q: How do you write small numbers in standard form?
faq.a: Move the point right until you have a number from 1 to under 10, and use a negative power. 0.0005 is 5 times 10 to the minus 4.
asks: How do I write 0.0005 in standard form?

faq.a: It saves writing zeros, avoids mistakes, and makes huge or tiny numbers easy to compare. Scientists use it every day.
Move the point 3 places to get 3.2, so 3,200 is 3.2 times 10 cubed.

facts: Light travels about 3 × 10⁸ metres per second.
The mass of the Earth is about 6 × 10²⁴ kg.
Standard form is also called scientific notation.

quiz.why: Move the point 5 places to get 6.2, so it is 6.2 times 10 to the 5.

wrong.1: 62 is bigger than 10, so this is not standard form.

quiz.why: The point moves 3 places right to get 3, so the power is minus 3.

wrong.2: 0.3 is less than 1, so this is not standard form.
